title: 生物学 · 7.11 蚂蚁颚与仿生夹具
source: 7.11 M1 生物学讲座 25-28 · Ant Mandibles

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Listen to a talk in a biology class.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: You've probably heard that ants can carry 50 times their own body weight.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Ants also, out on the front of their heads, they have strong mandibles.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Mandibles are like jaws, though ants use them like pincers, grippers like how humans use our thumb and index finger to pick things up.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Now, ants' mandibles, their inner surfaces, are covered in tiny hairs.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: And researchers working on biomimicry, biomimicry means imitating nature in human inventions, a group of researchers studying ant mandibles and their hairs recently wondered if they could use biomimicry with a robot gripper.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: So, a robot gripper is a device with flat plates that come together to pick things up.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: But it's difficult to pick up packaging with curved edges.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: So manufacturers often use grippers with three plates for stability.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: But three plates are bulky and harder to operate, you know, awkward.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: So, the researchers built a robot gripper with two plates with tiny artificial hairs, copying ants' mandibles, and another gripper with just the two smooth plates.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: They did an experiment with over 2,000 tests, an astonishing number, I think, comparing how well the grippers picked up items like a cereal box and a shampoo bottle.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Well, the hairy gripper was at least 29% better at grabbing and holding onto items.

segments.speaker: 讲师
segments.text: Its grip was more gentle and more secure.
